title: Fortastra and Hadrian join forces to streamline satellite production
summary: Fortastra, a Los Angeles startup focused on defending on-orbit infrastructure, is collaborating with Hadrian to enhance satellite production using precision machining and additive manufacturing.

title: H3 to launch next ispace lunar lander mission
summary: Japanese lunar lander developer ispace has chosen the H3 rocket to launch its next mission in 2028, marking Japan's first private lunar transportation system.

title: Boeing still working with NASA to schedule next Starliner flight
summary: Boeing is collaborating with NASA to finalize the schedule for the next CST-100 Starliner mission to the International Space Station. The flight, planned as a cargo mission, is part of ongoing efforts to resume Starliner operations.

title: Chinese startup raises funds for space situational awareness constellation, joining commercial SSA rush
summary: A Beijing-based startup raised $14 million to develop a satellite constellation for tracking orbital objects, contributing to China's expanding commercial space situational awareness (SSA) sector.

title: Swift reboost mission encounters attitude control problems
summary: A spacecraft launched to boost NASA's astrophysics satellite's orbit is facing attitude control issues that may threaten its mission. The Swift reboost mission, which began nearly a month ago, is encountering problems that could jeopardize its objectives.

title: ESA opens call to repurpose Gateway communications module
summary: The European Space Agency (ESA) is exploring the possibility of repurposing the Lunar Link communications module, originally built for NASA's paused Gateway space station. The initiative aims to assess the feasibility of adapting the system for new lunar or deep-space missions.

title: NASA selects successor to CAPSTONE lunar mission
summary: NASA has chosen Advanced Space to lead a follow-up mission to the CAPSTONE lunar smallsat, which will demonstrate rendezvous and proximity operations near the moon. The new mission aims to build on CAPSTONE's cislunar technology and operations.

title: Upper C-band auction offers another lift for GEO industry
summary: The FCC's upcoming auction of upper C-band spectrum is expected to generate over $6 billion, benefiting satellite operators and funding new geostationary spacecraft and transition costs.

title: Sphinx Defense wins $287 million contract for strategic satellite communications software
summary: Sphinx Defense has secured a $287 million contract to develop mission planning software for the U.S. Space Force's next-generation strategic communications satellites, known as ESS. This award highlights the growing focus on advanced satellite communication technologies within the defense sector.

title: Orbes unveils Exo-ORB and agreement with Symphony Space
summary: Orbes, a Southern California startup, unveiled Exo-ORB, a free-flying satellite, and announced an agreement to use it for imagery of Symphony Space's uncrewed station. The mission aims to gather data from the Symphony Space station.

title: X-ray spacecraft detects the 36-million-degree 'breath' of an ancient black hole
summary: Astronomers detected the extremely hot emissions from ancient quasars, which are powered by supermassive black holes. The X-ray spacecraft identified these 36-million-degree 'exhaust fumes' from the early universe.

title: July's full Buck Moon leads a mini planet parade through the summer sky tonight
summary: The July full moon, known as the Buck Moon, will rise tonight alongside a mini planet parade featuring Venus, Saturn, Mercury, and Mars. This celestial event offers a rare opportunity to observe multiple planets and the full moon together in the summer sky.

title: DJI Lito 1 drone review
summary: The DJI Lito 1 drone is praised for its entry-level features, including omnidirectional obstacle sensing and good image quality.

title: NASA fuels its next-gen Roman Space Telescope for August launch
summary: NASA has successfully fueled its next-generation Roman Space Telescope in preparation for its scheduled launch on August 30. The mission remains on track for the targeted date.

title: Our Milky Way galaxy appears to have flipped 90 degrees long ago. But why?
summary: The Milky Way galaxy may have flipped 90 degrees in its past due to a slowly rotating stellar halo. This event suggests a major but unknown occurrence in the galaxy's history.

title: SpaceX launches 24 Starlink satellites to orbit in wake of Starship test flight (video)
summary: SpaceX successfully launched 24 Starlink satellites into orbit using a Falcon 9 rocket from Vandenberg Space Force Base. The mission followed the recent Starship test flight.

title: ISS meets Venus in incredible daylight photo | Space photo of the day for July 28, 2026
summary: An astrophotographer captured a rare daytime image of the International Space Station passing near Venus. The photo highlights the ISS's orbital path against the bright planet in broad daylight.

title: BALLS on the moon: China set to launch Africa's 1st lunar science mission in 2029
summary: China is set to launch Africa's first lunar science mission in 2029, sending three spherical probes to the moon's south pole aboard its Chang'e 8 lander. This mission marks a significant step in international lunar exploration collaboration.

title: Ship 40’s flawless flight promotes next mission catch potential
summary: SpaceX's Starship Flight 13, featuring Ship 40, successfully completed its mission and returned intact, demonstrating the vehicle's reliability. This achievement paves the way for the next mission, which may involve catching the spacecraft mid-air.

title: Launch Preview: Falcon 9 and Chang Zheng rockets set to launch this week
summary: Five orbital launches are scheduled this week, including a Chang Zheng 6A rocket launch in China. SpaceX's Falcon 9 is also among the rockets set for launch.

title: Juno reveals surprising subsurface tempertures at Io, remarkably smooth surface
summary: NASA's Juno mission reveals surprising subsurface temperatures and a remarkably smooth surface on Jupiter's moon Io during two recent flybys. The findings challenge previous assumptions about the volcanic moon's geology.

title: Blue Origin to conduct New Glenn second stage hot fires on Stennis B-2 stand
summary: NASA and Blue Origin have finalized plans to conduct hot-fire tests for the second stage of the New Glenn rocket on the Stennis B-2 test stand. This marks a significant step in the development of Blue Origin's orbital launch vehicle.

title: Starship Flight 13 achieves new firsts for SpaceX
summary: Starship Flight 13, featuring Booster 20 and Ship 40, achieved new milestones for SpaceX on its third attempt. This marks another step forward in SpaceX's development of the Starship system.

title: Soyuz MS-29 crew arrives at ISS, U.S. EVA completes Canadarm2 repairs
summary: The Soyuz MS-29 crew successfully docked with the International Space Station (ISS), expanding the station's crew by three members. A U.S. extravehicular activity (EVA) was conducted to complete repairs on the Canadarm2 robotic arm.

title: Path to Starship Flight 13 requires additional Booster 20 test
summary: SpaceX aims for Starship Flight 13 no earlier than July 23, but additional testing of Booster 20 is required before the next attempt.

title: Falcon 9 to launch MRV-1 robotic servicing spacecraft for Northrop Grumman
summary: SpaceX's Falcon 9 is scheduled to launch the Mission Robotic Vehicle (MRV-1) robotic servicing spacecraft for Northrop Grumman from Florida.

title: Launch Preview: Falcon 9, Starship, and Chinese rockets scheduled to launch
summary: SpaceX is preparing for a new launch attempt of Starship Flight 13 after the previous attempt was aborted. Additionally, Falcon 9 and Chinese rockets are also scheduled to launch.

title: Making Progress: Relativity’s Terran R, Rocket Lab’s Neutron, and PLD Space’s Miura 5
summary: Relativity Space, Rocket Lab, and PLD Space are making progress with their new rocket developments: Terran R, Neutron, and Miura 5, respectively. While SpaceX's Starship has been in the spotlight, these companies continue advancing their launch vehicle programs.

title: TEC Business to Business website
summary: The news source is a B2B website focused on the technology and electronics industry, providing business-related content and insights.

title: ESA Delivers: 50 years booklet
summary: ESA celebrates 50 years with a booklet highlighting 50 major achievements. The publication marks five decades of the European Space Agency's contributions to space exploration and technology.

title: Earth and Proba-3’s Coronagraph play hide and seek
summary: ESA's Proba-3 mission will use two satellites to create an artificial solar eclipse, allowing the coronagraph to study the Sun's corona. The mission involves a game of hide and seek between Earth and the coronagraph.

title: Meet space startups at ESA’s Industry Space Days
summary: ESA's Industry Space Days event on 16–17 September at ESA-ESTEC in the Netherlands will feature startup companies showcasing innovative space technologies and fostering collaboration within Europe's space industry.

title: The silicon brains steering next-generation antennas
summary: Next-generation antennas are being enhanced with advanced silicon-based components to improve performance and efficiency. This technology is poised to revolutionize communication systems in the space industry.

title: Plato's electronics ready for space
summary: ESA's PLATO spacecraft has completed electromagnetic compatibility tests in the Maxwell Test Chamber, ensuring its electronics are fit for space. The mission is scheduled to launch on an Ariane 6 rocket in March 2027.

title: Test firing at brand new green chemical propulsion lab
summary: A new green chemical propulsion lab conducted its first test firing. This marks a significant step in developing environmentally friendly propulsion technologies for space missions.

title: Upcoming ESA–Industry events on CM25 implementation
summary: ESA is hosting events to present the follow-up to the CM25 meeting, focusing on planned activities and industrial opportunities. The events aim to inform and engage the industrial community on key thematic priorities.

title: We’re back: Proba-3 ready for more science
summary: The Proba-3 mission's Coronagraph spacecraft and ASPIICS instrument are fully operational, resuming formation flying to create artificial eclipses for scientific observations.

title: Outlier Space Raises $7.3M to Build New Zealand’s First Reentry Vehicle
summary: Outlier Space secured $7.35 million to develop New Zealand's first reentry vehicle for microgravity research, with a planned debut mission in 2028.

title: ESA taps Aalyria to build deep-space network hub
summary: ESA has selected Aalyria to construct a network-operations center for deep-space communication, enabling spacecraft to reliably share data across the solar system.

title: Space Science’s Golden Age Problem
summary: The White House OSTP released a comprehensive vision for the nation's research and development enterprise. The move aims to address challenges in space science's current 'golden age'.

title: Amazon Joins the Direct-to-Device Race
summary: Amazon has entered the direct-to-device satellite market by filing a request with the FCC to launch 5,105 low-Earth orbit satellites. This move positions Amazon as a competitor in the growing space-based connectivity sector.

title: New Report Maps Potential Futures for Africa’s Space Ecosystem
summary: A new report explores potential future developments for Africa's space ecosystem as the continent aims to establish itself as a significant player in the global space industry. The analysis highlights strategic opportunities and challenges for Africa's growing space ambitions.

title: Rocket Lab Expands to Alaska with $266M Launch Contract
summary: Rocket Lab is establishing a new launch site at the Pacific Spaceport Complex-Alaska in Kodiak, with launches expected to begin by the end of this year. The expansion is supported by a $266 million launch contract.

title: ORBES Unveils Exo-ORB Maintenance Spacecraft
summary: ORBES introduced the Exo-ORB Maintenance Spacecraft, a ~12U, sub-26-kg spacecraft designed for on-orbit inspection and maintenance. The spacecraft is intended to launch onboard customer infrastructure for ready-to-use deployment.

title: Starship Sticks the Water Landing on Flight 13
summary: SpaceX successfully completed the 13th test flight of its Starship rocket, achieving the first intact water landing. The mission marked a significant milestone in the rocket's development.

title: ESA Puts €65M Behind Europe’s First Lunar Ice Rover
summary: ESA has committed €65 million to Europe's first lunar polar ice exploration rover mission, led by ispace-Europe. This marks a significant step for Europe in lunar exploration.

title: Lunar Outpost Plans to Fly NVIDIA Chips to the Moon
summary: Lunar Outpost is planning to send NVIDIA chips to the Moon, combining the chip industry's advancements with lunar exploration efforts. This move highlights the intersection of technology and space missions in the new Moon race.

title: Rocket Lab Nabs Largest Launch Award; Establishing Site In Alaska
summary: Rocket Lab secured its largest launch contract worth $266 million from the Space Force, involving at least 12 suborbital missions. The company is also establishing a new launch site in Alaska.

title: Eutelsat Details IRIS² MoU With Poland
summary: Eutelsat has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Poland to support Europe's IRIS² satellite program, focusing on secure satellite development. The collaboration aims to enhance Europe's satellite infrastructure.

title: Impulse Space Details its First Electric Propulsion System
summary: Impulse Space has unveiled its first electric propulsion system, named Electra, designed for long-duration space operations. This development follows a year of exploration into the technology.

title: Skywave to Add Iridium SBS Data Service Into Industrial IoT Offering
summary: Skywave and Iridium have formed a strategic partnership to integrate Iridium's Short Burst Data (SBD) services into Skywave's industrial IoT offerings for heavy equipment OEM customers. This collaboration marks the first time Iridium's SBD services are being added to Skywave's portfolio.

title: Virgin Media O2 Exec Explains Strategic Approach to Direct-to-Device With O2 Satellite
summary: Virgin Media O2, a major U.K. mobile operator, has launched O2 Satellite, a direct-to-device service enabled by satellite technology. An executive explains the company's strategic approach to this new offering.

title: Space-Based Data Centers: Inside the Race to Move Compute to Orbit
summary: The space industry is exploring the concept of space-based data centers to meet the growing demand for computing power driven by AI. Companies are racing to move some data center infrastructure into orbit to leverage the unique advantages of space.

title: SES Space & Defense Wins Space Station Connectivity Deal With Starlab
summary: SES Space & Defense will collaborate with Starlab to develop a communication architecture for continuous connectivity on the Starlab space station. This deal highlights advancements in space station infrastructure and connectivity solutions.

title: Amazon Leo Files for 5,105 Satellites in Globalstar Spectrum for D2D
summary: Amazon has filed with the FCC to launch a Direct-to-Device constellation of up to 5,105 satellites using spectrum acquired from Globalstar. This move aims to expand Amazon's satellite-based connectivity services.

title: SES Set to Receive $5.6B in Incentive Payments for C-Band Clearing
summary: SES is set to receive $5.6 billion in incentive payments for clearing the C-band, while Eutelsat will receive $504 million, according to the FCC's final C-band plan.

title: Via Satellite Rising Stars of 2026
summary: Via Satellite announces the third class of 25 Rising Stars for 2026, highlighting young professionals shaping the future of the space and satellite industry.
